title: slot lifecycle evictor and smoothed-pin policy to reduce KV churn
author: Aditi Rao
description:
Summary: Implements a SlotLifecycleManager and a smoothed-pin eviction policy to reduce churn in the paged KV block manager. The change introduces a per-CPU recyclable slot pool, an EWMA-based 'smoothed' pin score for pins that briefly spike, and low-latency background compaction windows to avoid interfering with hot-path token generation. Motivation: Recent canaries and perf lab runs showed that short-lived hot prefixes and bursty access patterns cause repeated pin/unpin churn, increasing CPU time in the allocator and causing tail latency spikes. This PR reduces the frequency of hard evictions and makes pin decisions more stable under bursty workloads.

Design & key changes: - New component: src/kv/slot_lifecycle.rs (SlotLifecycleManager). Responsible for tracking slot states (hot, warm, cold) and scheduling reclaim/compaction work off the critical path. - Smoothed-pin policy: we use a lightweight EWMA on access timestamps to compute a pin_score per slot. Short bursts raise the score but decay quickly; the eviction decision uses a delta threshold to avoid immediate unpin on transient drops. - Per-CPU recyclable slot pools: reduce global contention by returning freed slots to a per-cpu ring buffer; global pooling only used when per-cpu pools are low. - Deferred compaction windows: compaction and slab merge tasks are scheduled by the lifecycle manager and throttled by realtime load signals (continuous batching backlog and CPU utilization). - Config knobs: kv.slot_lifecycle.enabled, kv.smoothed_pin.alpha, kv.percpu_pool_size, kv.compaction.load_threshold. Defaults chosen to be conservative and disabled in private installer until canary completes.

Commits (high-level): - a1b3d7c: Add SlotLifecycleManager scaffolding, metrics and basic lifecycle state machine - 5f2e9a1: Implement smoothed-pin EWMA, per-cpu recycler and fastpath for hot slots - c9d1f4b: Add benches, unit tests, docs, feature flags and rollout knobs

Files changed (high-level): - src/kv/slot_lifecycle.rs (new) - src/kv/allocator.rs (policy hooks and interfaces) - src/kv/slot_table.rs (pin/unpin instrumentation) - runtime/batching/scheduler.rs (load signal hook) - benches/kv_reuse_bench.rs (bench harness) - tests/slot_lifecycle_test.rs (unit + integration) - docs/perf/kv_strategy.md - config/defaults.toml

Benchmarks & results (perf lab): All numbers are median over 10 runs on a Dedicated 4xA100 canary with production-like trace. Workload: mixed read-heavy prefix cache with bursts.
- Throughput (tokens/sec): +18% on steady-state multi-client load. - P99 generation latency: -12% on KV-hit-heavy profiles. - Eviction CPU cycles: -34% measured in allocator flame graphs. - Scheduling contention (lock hold time in allocator): -27%. - Memory fragmentation (internal metric): -8% reduction after longer runs.

Testing & validation: - Unit tests for lifecycle transitions and EWMA math. - Integration tests for per-cpu recycler under concurrency (stress). - Perf bench added and run in benchmark-lab with CI artifacts attached. - Canary rollout plan: enable feature flag for 5% of Dedicated capacity, monitor allocator CPU, p99 tail, and KV hit ratio for 48 hours, then expand.

Rollout & rollback plan: Feature gated. Default OFF for Private installer until we complete enterprise canary (expected 2 weeks). Rollback toggles via kv.slot_lifecycle.enabled=false which immediately returns behavior to previous allocator fastpath. In-flight requests are not affected; background tasks will drain.

Observability & metrics added: - kv.slot_lifecycle.evictions - kv.slot_lifecycle.reclaimed_slots_per_sec - kv.slot_lifecycle.pin_score_ewma_p50/p95 - allocator.percpu_pool_hits

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-2345) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Benchmarks in perf lab - [x] Config knobs and PRD/rollout plan - [x] Docs updated

Review conversation (selected): - Noah Kim: "Can you explain why EWMA and not a tiny TTL? What's the expected sensitivity tradeoff?" - Aditi: "EWMA gives us fine-grained sensitivity control and smooth decay without allocating per-slot timers. The alpha is configurable; a TTL would need busy timers or coarse time buckets which had higher overhead in benchmarks." - Ethan Brooks: "Per-cpu pool sounds good, but what about long-tail starving and stealing?" - Aditi: "Pools can be stolen by the global pool when low; stealing is implemented with an O(1) batch move to amortize cost. Tests exercise steal under heavy allocations." - Priya Nair: "Please add a knob to disable background compaction in private installer — I see you did that in defaults, thanks." - Priya (approval): "LGTM after small comment about metric tagging."

CI: All checks passed (unit, integration, lint, benchmark job). One flaky test in earlier run (tests/slot_lifecycle_test::concurrency_stress) failed once and was rerun and passed; added additional backoff in test harness to reduce flakiness.

Merge & follow-ups: Squash-merged to main on 2025-11-20. Follow-up tickets created: ENG-2501 (observability dashboard), ENG-2502 (canary automation for slot_lifecycle), and a small perf tweak ENG-2503 to expose per-cpu pool stats to the console.
release_notes: Introduces a SlotLifecycleManager and smoothed-pin policy to reduce allocator churn and tail latency. Improves throughput and reduces allocator CPU in KV-heavy workflows. Feature-gated and rolled out via canary. Config knobs: kv.slot_lifecycle.*, kv.smoothed_pin.*.
